claims.text: A functionally graded multilayer HEA coating will provide superior elevated-temperature tribo-corrosion resistance compared with a conventional uniform HEA coating.
A functionally graded multilayer HEA coating will provide superior elevated-temperature tribo-corrosion resistance compared with standard structural alloys.
42-CrMo steel without prior surface treatment can serve as the substrate for the proposed coating.
A W-V-Ta-Ti-Cr HEA coating can be deposited on 42-CrMo steel by laser cladding.
Controlling or increasing Cr content in a W-based WVTaTiCr coating can refine its grains and improve hardness, high-temperature oxidation resistance, and corrosion resistance.
A Cr-controlled W-based HEA top layer will have low friction and high wear resistance.
An underlying HEA sub-layer can be engineered to provide enhanced oxidation and corrosion resistance.
The proposed material is intended to operate at approximately 450–650 degrees Celsius in a NaCl-containing corrosive environment.
The proposed coating will resist combined corrosion and dynamic sliding wear under these conditions.
The graded multilayer coating will possess refined grains and controlled interdiffusion at its interfaces.
Controlled interdiffusion in the graded structure will promote a stable protective oxide layer enriched in oxidation-resistant elements in the sub-layer.
The hard top layer will minimize sliding-induced mechanical damage, friction, and dislocation-induced degradation.
The sub-layer will form and maintain a protective oxide scale that mitigates high-temperature corrosion.
The functionally graded interface will improve adhesion and reduce oxide or coating spallation.
Combining the wear-resistant top layer, protective sub-layer, and graded interface will synergistically suppress tribo-corrosion.
The multilayer coating will reduce wear rate and friction coefficient relative to a conventional single-layer coating.
The multilayer coating will reduce corrosion or oxidation rates relative to conventional coatings or structural alloys.
Reduced wear and corrosion will significantly extend component lifespan under tribo-corrosive conditions.
Temperatures above 650 degrees Celsius, extreme friction forces, or poorly optimized layer thicknesses and interdiffusion barriers may cause coating delamination and eliminate the improvement.
